title.zh: 新唐書卷七十一 表第十一上 宰相世系一上

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 唐為國久，傳世多，而諸臣亦各修其家法，務以門族相高。

translations.literal: Tang endured as a state for a long time, with many generations transmitted, while the various ministers also each cultivated their family rules, striving to exalt their clans and kin groups.
translations.idiomatic: Tang endured as a dynasty for many generations, and its ministers each upheld their own family codes, striving to exalt their clans and kin groups.

sentences.zh: 其材子賢孫不殞其世德，或父子相繼居相位，或累數世而屢顯，或終唐之世不絕。

translations.literal: Their gifted sons and worthy grandsons did not let their inherited virtue perish; some fathers and sons succeeded one another in the chancellorship, some rose to prominence generation after generation, and some never died out throughout the entire Tang period.
translations.idiomatic: Their gifted sons and worthy grandsons did not let their inherited virtue fade; some fathers and sons held the chancellorship in succession, some rose to prominence across many generations, and some lines never died out throughout the Tang.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，其亦盛矣！

translations.literal: Alas, how flourishing they were!
translations.idiomatic: Ah—what a flourishing age it was!

sentences.zh: 然其所以盛衰者，雖由功德薄厚，亦在其子孫。

translations.literal: Yet the reason for their rise and fall, though it lay in the thickness or thinness of merit and virtue, also rested in their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether they flourished or declined depended not only on the weight of merit and virtue, but also on their descendants.

sentences.zh: 作〈宰相世系表〉。

translations.literal: Therefore the Genealogical Tables of Chancellors are compiled.〉
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Genealogical Tables of Chancellors are presented here.〉

sentences.zh: 裴裴氏出自風姓。

translations.literal: The Pei clan derives from the Feng surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Pei clan traces its origin to the Feng surname.

sentences.zh: 顓頊裔孫大業生女華，女華生大費，大費生皐陶，皐陶生伯益，賜姓嬴氏。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu's descendant Daye begot Nühua; Nühua begot Dafei; Dafei begot Gao Yao; Gao Yao begot Bo Yi, who was granted the surname Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu's descendant Daye had a daughter Nühua, who bore Dafei; Dafei bore Gao Yao; Gao Yao bore Bo Yi, who received the surname Ying.

sentences.zh: 生大廉，大廉五世孫曰仲衍，仲衍四世孫曰軒，軒生潏，潏生飛廉，飛廉生惡來，惡來生女防，女防生旁皐，旁皐生太几，太几生大駱，大駱生非子，周孝王使養馬汧渭之間， 以馬蕃息，封之於秦為附庸，使續嬴氏，號曰秦嬴。

translations.literal: He begot Dalian; Dalian's fifth-generation descendant was called Zhongyan; Zhongyan's fourth-generation descendant was called Xuan; Xuan begot Yu; Yu begot Feilian; Feilian begot Elai; Elai begot Nüfang; Nüfang begot Panggao; Panggao begot Taiji; Taiji begot Daluo; Daluo begot Feizi. King Xiao of Zhou had him raise horses between the Qian and Wei rivers; because the horses multiplied, he was enfeoffed in Qin as a subordinate state, made to continue the Ying clan, and styled Qin Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi had a son Dalian; five generations later came Zhongyan, and four generations after him Xuan. Xuan's line ran through Yu, Feilian, Elai, Nüfang, Panggao, Taiji, and Daluo to Feizi. King Xiao of Zhou set Feizi to breed horses between the Qian and Wei; when the herds flourished, Qin was enfeoffed as a vassal state to carry on the Ying line, styled Qin Ying.

sentences.zh: 非子之支孫封𨛬鄉，因以為氏，今聞喜𨛬城是也。

translations.literal: A collateral descendant of Feizi was enfeoffed at Xiang township and took it as his clan name; the present Xiang walled town in Wenxi is that place.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral branch of Feizi's line was enfeoffed at Xiang township and took that name as their clan; the Xiang walled town in present-day Wenxi is that site.

sentences.zh: 六世孫陵，當周僖王之時封為解邑君，乃去「邑」從「衣」為裴。

translations.literal: The sixth-generation descendant Ling, in the time of King Xi of Zhou, was enfeoffed as Lord of Xie township; he then removed "township" and took "garment" to form the surname Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations later, Ling was enfeoffed as Lord of Xie township under King Xi of Zhou; he dropped the "township" element and took the "garment" radical, forming the surname Pei.

sentences.zh: 裴，衣長貌。

translations.literal: Pei means the long appearance of a garment.
translations.idiomatic: Pei denotes the flowing length of a robe.

sentences.zh: 一云晉平公封顓頊之孫鍼於周川之裴中，號裴君，疑不可辨。

translations.literal: One account says Duke Ping of Jin enfeoffed Zhuanxu's grandson Zhen in Pei of Zhou River, styled Lord Pei; this is doubtful and cannot be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Another account holds that Duke Ping of Jin enfeoffed Zhuanxu's grandson Zhen at Pei on the Zhou River and styled him Lord Pei—but this tradition is doubtful and cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 陵裔孫蓋，漢水衡都尉、侍中，九世孫燉煌太守遵，自雲中從光武平隴蜀，徙居河東安邑，安順之際徙聞喜。

translations.literal: Ling's descendant Gai was Commandant of the Water Balance for Han and Palace Attendant; his ninth-generation descendant Zun, Governor of Dunhuang, followed from Yunzhong with Emperor Guangwu to pacify Long and Shu, moved to Anyi in Hedong, and during the An-Shun era moved to Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's descendant Gai served Han as Commandant of the Water Balance and Palace Attendant. Nine generations later, Zun, Governor of Dunhuang, followed Guangwu from Yunzhong in the pacification of Long and Shu, settled at Anyi in Hedong, and during the An-Shun reigns moved the family to Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 曾孫曄，幷州刺史、度遼將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Ye was Governor of Bing Province and General Who Crosses the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's great-grandson Ye served as Governor of Bing Province and General Who Crosses the Liao.

sentences.zh: 子茂字巨光，靈帝時歷郡守、尚書，率諸將討李傕有功，封陽吉平侯。

translations.literal: His son Mao, styled Juguan, during Emperor Ling's reign served as prefect and as Minister; leading generals against Li Jue with merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangjiping.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's son Mao, styled Juguan, held prefectural and ministerial posts under Emperor Ling; for leading troops against Li Jue he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yangjiping.

sentences.zh: 三子：潛、徽、輯。

translations.literal: Three sons: Qian, Hui, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Qian, Hui, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 西眷裴出自陽吉平侯茂長子徽，字文秀，魏冀州刺史、蘭陵武公，以其子孫多仕西涼者，故號西眷。

translations.literal: The Western Branch Pei derives from Mao, Marquis of Yangjiping, his eldest son Hui, styled Wenxiu, Governor of Ji Province of Wei and Duke Wu of Lanling; because many descendants served in Western Liang, they are therefore called the Western Branch.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Branch of the Pei clan stems from Mao's eldest son Hui, styled Wenxiu, who served Wei as Governor of Ji Province and Duke Wu of Lanling. Because many of his descendants held office in Western Liang, the line is called the Western Branch.

sentences.zh: 四子：黎、康、楷、綽。

translations.literal: Four sons: Li, Kang, Kai, and Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had four sons: Li, Kang, Kai, and Chuo.

sentences.zh: 黎字伯宗，一名演，游擊將軍、祕書監。

translations.literal: Li, styled Bozong, also named Yan, was General of Rapid Attack and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li, styled Bozong (also called Yan), served as General of Rapid Attack and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二子粹、苞。

translations.literal: Two sons: Cui and Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Li had two sons: Cui and Bao.

sentences.zh: 粹，晉武威太守。

translations.literal: Cui was Governor of Wuwei under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Cui served Jin as Governor of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 二子：詵、暅。

translations.literal: Two sons: Shen and Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui had two sons: Shen and Jiong.

sentences.zh: 詵，太常卿，避地涼州，及苻堅克河西，復還解縣，生劭，劭生和，和生鍾，鍾生景惠。

translations.literal: Shen was Minister of Ceremonies; he fled to Liangzhou, and when Fu Jian conquered Hexi he returned to Jie county; he begot Shao; Shao begot He; He begot Zhong; Zhong begot Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, Minister of Ceremonies, took refuge in Liangzhou; when Fu Jian conquered Hexi he returned to Jie county. His line ran through Shao, He, and Zhong to Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 洗馬裴出自粹子暅。

translations.literal: The Xima Pei derive from Cui's son Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: The Xima branch of the Pei clan stems from Cui's son Jiong.

sentences.zh: 暅生慬，自河西歸桑梓，居解縣洗馬川，號洗馬裴，仕前秦大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Jiong begot Qin, who returned from Hexi to his native place, dwelt at Xima River in Jie county, was styled Xima Pei, and served Former Qin as Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's son Qin came back from Hexi to his homeland, settled on the Xima River in Jie county, and gave the line the name Xima Pei; he served Former Qin as Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 二子：天恩、天壽。

translations.literal: Two sons: Tian'en and Tianshou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had two sons: Tian'en and Tianshou.

sentences.zh: 南來吳裴出自黎第二子苞。

translations.literal: The Southern-Coming Wu Pei derive from Li's second son Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern-Coming Wu branch of the Pei stems from Li's second son Bao.

sentences.zh: 苞三子：軫、丕、彬。

translations.literal: Bao had three sons: Zhen, Pi, and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had three sons: Zhen, Pi, and Bin.

sentences.zh: 軫生嗣，嗣西涼武都太守。

translations.literal: Zhen begot Si; Si was Governor of Wudu under Western Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's son Si served Western Liang as Governor of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 三子：邕、奣、策。

translations.literal: Three sons: Yong, Weng, and Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Si had three sons: Yong, Weng, and Ce.

sentences.zh: 邕度江居襄陽，生順宗。

translations.literal: Yong crossed the river and dwelt at Xiangyang; he begot Shunzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong crossed the Yangzi and settled at Xiangyang; his son was Shunzong.

sentences.zh: 順宗三子：叔寶、叔業、令寶。

translations.literal: Shunzong had three sons: Shubao, Shuye, and Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong had three sons: Shubao, Shuye, and Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 叔業，齊南兗州刺史，初歸北，號南來吳裴，事後魏，豫州刺史、蘭陵郡公，謚忠武。

translations.literal: Shuye was Governor of Southern Yanzhou under Qi; when he first returned to the north he was styled Southern-Coming Wu Pei; he served Later Wei as Governor of Yu Province and Duke of Lanling, posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye, Governor of Southern Yanzhou under Qi, was the first to return north and gave the line the name Southern-Coming Wu Pei. Serving Later Wei, he became Governor of Yu Province and Duke of Lanling, posthumously titled Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 子蒨之、芬之、簡之、英之、藹之。

translations.literal: Sons: Qianzhi, Fenzhi, Jianzhi, Yingzhi, and Aizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Qianzhi, Fenzhi, Jianzhi, Yingzhi, and Aizhi.

sentences.zh: 令寶二子：彥先、彥遠。

translations.literal: Lingbao had two sons: Yanxian and Yanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbao had two sons: Yanxian and Yanyuan.

sentences.zh: 彥遠生鑒，鑒生獻。

translations.literal: Yanyuan begot Jian; Jian begot Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyuan's line continued through Jian to Xian.

sentences.zh: 中眷裴氏出自嗣中子奣，晉太尉宋公版諮議參軍、幷州別駕，號中眷。

translations.literal: The Central Branch Pei derive from Si's middle son Weng, Staff Adviser to the Duke of Song, Grand Marshal of Jin, and Bingzhou Aide; he was styled the Central Branch.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Branch of the Pei stems from Si's middle son Weng, who served Jin as Staff Adviser to the Duke of Song and Bingzhou Aide; the line is called the Central Branch.

sentences.zh: 三子：萬虎、雙虎、三虎。

translations.literal: Three sons: Wanhu, Shuanghu, and Sanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Weng had three sons: Wanhu, Shuanghu, and Sanhu.

sentences.zh: 苞第三子丕。

translations.literal: Bao's third son was Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's third son was Pi.

sentences.zh: 丕孫定宗。

translations.literal: Pi's grandson was Dingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's grandson was Dingzong.

sentences.zh: 定宗，涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Dingzong was Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong served as Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 生訛，後魏冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He begot E; E was Champion General under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong's son E served Later Wei as Champion General.

sentences.zh: 生遼，太原太守、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He begot Liao; Liao was Governor of Taiyuan and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: E's son Liao was Governor of Taiyuan and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 生纂，纂正平太守、鄜西公。

translations.literal: He begot Zuan; Zuan was Governor of Zhengping and Duke of Fuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liao's son Zuan was Governor of Zhengping and Duke of Fuxi.

sentences.zh: 四子：舒、嗣、秀、詢。

translations.literal: Four sons: Shu, Si, Xiu, and Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had four sons: Shu, Si, Xiu, and Xun.

sentences.zh: 舒，周車騎將軍、元氏公。

translations.literal: Shu was General of Chariots and Cavalry under Zhou and Duke of Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shu served Northern Zhou as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 生昂。

translations.literal: He begot Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's son was Ang.

sentences.zh: 生玄運，濮州刺史。

translations.literal: He begot Xuanyun; Xuanyun was Governor of Pu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's son Xuanyun was Governor of Pu Province.

sentences.zh: 生季友，司門郞中、太子僕。

translations.literal: He begot Jiyou; Jiyou was Director of the Gate Office and Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyun's son Jiyou was Director of the Gate Office and Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 生武，武曾孫訢。

translations.literal: He begot Wu; Wu's great-grandson was Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou's son Wu was ancestor to the great-grandson Xin.

sentences.zh: 東眷裴出自茂第三子輯，號東眷。

translations.literal: The Eastern Branch Pei derive from Mao's third son Ji, styled the Eastern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Branch of the Pei stems from Mao's third son Ji and is called the Eastern Branch.

sentences.zh: 生潁，潁司隸校尉。

translations.literal: He begot Ying; Ying was Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Ying served as Metropolitan Commandant.

sentences.zh: 生武，字文應，晉大將軍、玄菟太守，永嘉末，避地平州。

translations.literal: He begot Wu, styled Wenying, Great General and Governor of Xuantu under Jin; at the end of the Yongjia era he fled to Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's son Wu, styled Wenying, was Great General and Governor of Xuantu under Jin; at the end of the Yongjia era he took refuge in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二子：開、湛。

translations.literal: Two sons: Kai and Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had two sons: Kai and Zhan.

sentences.zh: 開字景舒，仕慕容氏，太常卿、祭酒。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Jingshu, served the Murong clan as Minister of Ceremonies and Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, styled Jingshu, served the Murong as Minister of Ceremonies and Libationer.

sentences.zh: 三子：原、成、範。

translations.literal: Three sons: Yuan, Cheng, and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai had three sons: Yuan, Cheng, and Fan.

sentences.zh: 範字仁則，河南太守。

translations.literal: Fan, styled Renze, was Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, styled Renze, was Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 四子：韜、沖、湛、綏。

translations.literal: Four sons: Tao, Chong, Zhan, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had four sons: Tao, Chong, Zhan, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 沖字太寧，後秦幷州刺史、夷陵子。

translations.literal: Chong, styled Taining, was Governor of Bing Province under Later Qin and Viscount of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, styled Taining, served Later Qin as Governor of Bing Province and held the title Viscount of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 五子：道子、道護、道大、道會、道賜。

translations.literal: Five sons: Daozi, Daohu, Daoda, Daohui, and Daoci.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had five sons: Daozi, Daohu, Daoda, Daohui, and Daoci.

sentences.zh: 道子字復泰，本州別駕，從劉裕入關，事魏，南梁州刺史、義昌順伯。

translations.literal: Daozi, styled Futai, was Aide of his native province; following Liu Yu into the passes, he served Wei as Governor of Southern Liang Province and Baron Shun of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi, styled Futai, was Aide of his home province; he followed Liu Yu through the passes into Wei service as Governor of Southern Liang and Baron Shun of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 三子：德歡、恩立、輔立。

translations.literal: Three sons: Dehuan, Enli, and Fuli.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi had three sons: Dehuan, Enli, and Fuli.

sentences.zh: 德歡一名度，豫鄭廣坊四州刺史，謚曰康。

translations.literal: Dehuan, also named Du, was Governor of the four provinces Yu, Zheng, Guang, and Fang; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Dehuan, also called Du, governed the four provinces of Yu, Zheng, Guang, and Fang; his posthumous title was Kang.

sentences.zh: 二子：澄、禮。

translations.literal: Two sons: Cheng and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Dehuan had two sons: Cheng and Li.

sentences.zh: 道護二子：次愛、祖念。

translations.literal: Daohu had two sons: Ci'ai and Zunian.
translations.idiomatic: Daohu had two sons: Ci'ai and Zunian.

sentences.zh: 祖念生弘陁，後魏聞喜公。

translations.literal: Zunian begot Hongtuo; Hongtuo was Duke of Wenxi under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zunian's son Hongtuo was Duke of Wenxi under Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 生鴻琳，易郡太守。

translations.literal: He begot Honglin; Honglin was Governor of Yi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hongtuo's son Honglin was Governor of Yi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 生客兒。

translations.literal: He begot Ke'er.
translations.idiomatic: Honglin's son was Ke'er.

sentences.zh: 裴氏定著五房：一曰西眷裴，二曰洗馬裴，三曰南來吳裴，四曰中眷裴，五曰東眷裴。

translations.literal: The Pei clan is definitively divided into five houses: first the Western Branch Pei, second the Xima Pei, third the Southern-Coming Wu Pei, fourth the Central Branch Pei, and fifth the Eastern Branch Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The Pei clan is firmly divided into five branches: the Western Branch, the Xima branch, the Southern-Coming Wu branch, the Central Branch, and the Eastern Branch.

sentences.zh: 宰相十七人。

translations.literal: Seventeen chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were seventeen chancellors.

sentences.zh: 西眷有寂、矩；

translations.literal: The Western Branch had Ji and Ju;
translations.idiomatic: The Western Branch produced Ji and Ju;

sentences.zh: 洗馬有談、炎；

translations.literal: the Xima had Tan and Yan;
translations.idiomatic: the Xima branch Tan and Yan;

sentences.zh: 南來吳有耀卿、行本、坦；

translations.literal: the Southern-Coming Wu had Yaoqing, Xingben, and Tan;
translations.idiomatic: the Southern-Coming Wu branch Yaoqing, Xingben, and Tan;

sentences.zh: 中眷有光庭、遵慶、樞、贄；

translations.literal: the Central Branch had Guangting, Zunqing, Shu, and Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: the Central Branch Guangting, Zunqing, Shu, and Zhi;

sentences.zh: 東眷有居道、休、澈、垍、冕、度。

translations.literal: the Eastern Branch had Judao, Xiu, Che, Ji, Mian, and Du.
translations.idiomatic: and the Eastern Branch Judao, Xiu, Che, Ji, Mian, and Du.

sentences.zh: 劉漢劉氏劉氏出自祁姓。

translations.literal: Liu of Han: The Liu clan derives from the Qi surname.
translations.idiomatic: Liu of Han: The Liu clan traces its origin to the Qi surname.

sentences.zh: 帝堯陶唐氏子孫生子有文在手曰：「劉累」，因以為名。

translations.literal: A descendant of Emperor Yao of the Taotang clan begot a son with writing on his hand reading "Liu Lei," and therefore took it as his name.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Emperor Yao of the Taotang line had a son born with characters on his palm reading "Liu Lei," and took that as his name.

sentences.zh: 能擾龍，事夏為御龍氏，在商為豕韋氏，在周封為杜伯，亦稱唐杜氏。

translations.literal: He could tame dragons; serving Xia he was styled Dragon-Tamer; under Shang he was the Pig-Wei clan; under Zhou he was enfeoffed as Duke of Du, also called the Tang-Du clan.
translations.idiomatic: He could tame dragons; under Xia he was called Dragon-Tamer; under Shang the Pig-Wei clan; under Zhou he was enfeoffed Duke of Du, also known as the Tang-Du line.

sentences.zh: 至宣王，滅其國。

translations.literal: When it reached King Xuan, he destroyed their state.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan of Zhou destroyed their state.

sentences.zh: 其子隰叔奔晉為士師，生士蒍。

translations.literal: His son Xishu fled to Jin and became Master of the Warriors; he begot Shi Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xishu fled to Jin as Master of the Warriors and had a son Shi Yan.

sentences.zh: 蒍生成伯缺，缺生士會。

translations.literal: Yan begot Cheng; Cheng begot Bo Que; Que begot Shi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's line ran through Cheng and Bo Que to Shi Hui.

sentences.zh: 會適秦，歸晉，有子留於秦，自為劉氏。

translations.literal: Hui went to Qin and returned to Jin; a son remained in Qin and styled himself the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui went to Qin and later returned to Jin, but a son who stayed behind in Qin became the founder of the Liu line.

sentences.zh: 生明，明生遠，遠生陽，十世孫，戰國時獲於魏，遂為魏大夫。

translations.literal: He begot Ming; Ming begot Yuan; Yuan begot Yang, the tenth-generation descendant; during the Warring States he was taken captive by Wei and thus became a grandee of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That line continued through Ming and Yuan to Yang, the tenth-generation descendant, who was captured by Wei in the Warring States period and became a Wei grandee.

sentences.zh: 秦滅魏，徙大梁，生清，徙居沛。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Wei they moved to Daliang; he begot Qing; Qing moved to dwell at Pei.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin conquered Wei the family moved to Daliang; Yang's descendant Qing later settled at Pei.

sentences.zh: 生仁，號豐公。

translations.literal: He begot Ren, styled Duke of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's son Ren was known as Duke of Feng.

sentences.zh: 生煓，字執嘉。

translations.literal: He begot Juan, styled Zhijia.
translations.idiomatic: Ren's son Juan was styled Zhijia.

sentences.zh: 生四子：伯、仲、邦、交。

translations.literal: He begot four sons: Bo, Zhong, Bang, and Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Juan had four sons: Bo, Zhong, Bang, and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 邦，漢高祖也。

translations.literal: Bang was Emperor Gaozu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Bang was Emperor Gaozu of Han.

sentences.zh: 高祖七世孫宣帝，生楚孝王嚻，嚻生思王衍，衍生紆，紆生居巢侯般，字伯興。

translations.literal: Gaozu's seventh-generation descendant was Emperor Xuan; he begot King Xiao of Chu Xi; Xi begot King Si Yan; Yan begot Yu; Yu begot Marquis of Juchao Ban, styled Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after Gaozu came Emperor Xuan, whose line ran through King Xiao of Chu Xi, King Si Yan, and Yu to Marquis of Juchao Ban, styled Boxing.

sentences.zh: 般生愷，字伯豫，太尉、司空。

translations.literal: Ban begot Kai, styled Boyu, Grand Marshal and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ban's son Kai, styled Boyu, served as Grand Marshal and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 生茂，字叔盛，司空、太中大夫，徙居叢亭里。

translations.literal: He begot Mao, styled Shusheng, Minister of Works and Grand Master of the Palace, who moved to dwell at Congting Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's son Mao, styled Shusheng, was Minister of Works and Grand Master of the Palace and moved the family to Congting Lane.

sentences.zh: 愷六世孫訥，晉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Kai's sixth-generation descendant Ne was Metropolitan Commandant under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations after Kai came Ne, Metropolitan Commandant under Jin.

sentences.zh: 孫憲生羨。

translations.literal: His grandson Xian begot Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's grandson Xian had a son also named Xian.

sentences.zh: 羨二子：敏、該。

translations.literal: Xian had two sons: Min and Gai.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had two sons: Min and Gai.

sentences.zh: 敏從子僧利。

translations.literal: Min's collateral nephew was Sengli.
translations.idiomatic: Min's collateral nephew was Sengli.

sentences.zh: 京兆武功劉氏，本出彭城，後周有石州刺史懿。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Wugong in Jingzhao originally came from Pengcheng; under Later Zhou there was Yi, Governor of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu of Wugong in Jingzhao originally hailed from Pengcheng; under Later Zhou one Yi served as Governor of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 彭城劉氏又有劉升。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Pengcheng also had Liu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Pengcheng Liu line also included Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 尉氏劉氏出自漢章帝子河間孝王開，世居樂城，十世孫通徙居尉氏。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Weishi derives from Emperor Zhang of Han's son, King Xiao of Hejian Kai; they dwelt for generations at Lecheng; the tenth-generation descendant Tong moved to dwell at Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: The Weishi Liu stem from King Xiao of Hejian Kai, son of Emperor Zhang of Han; the family lived at Lecheng for generations until the tenth-generation descendant Tong moved to Weishi.

sentences.zh: 臨淮劉氏出自漢世祖光武皇帝子廣陵思王荊。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Linhuai derives from Emperor Guangwu, Founder of Han, his son King Si of Guangling Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Linhuai Liu trace their line to King Si of Guangling Jing, son of Emperor Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 子俞鄉元侯平，平生彪，襲封，事繼母以孝聞，世號仁義侯。

translations.literal: His son Ping, Marquis Yuan of Yuxiang, in life was Biao; he inherited the enfeoffment; serving his stepmother he was famed for filial piety and was styled by the age the Marquis of Benevolence and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son Ping, Marquis Yuan of Yuxiang, was known in life as Biao; he inherited the title and won renown for filial devotion to his stepmother, earning the popular name Marquis of Benevolence and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 生玄，玄生熙，魏尚書郎。

translations.literal: He begot Xuan; Xuan begot Xi, Lang of the Masters of Writing under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had a son Xuan, whose son Xi served Wei as a Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 熙生述，東平太守。

translations.literal: Xi begot Shu, Governor of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Shu served as Governor of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 述生建，晉永城令，世居臨淮。

translations.literal: Shu begot Jian, Magistrate of Yongcheng under Jin; the clan dwelt for generations at Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's son Jian was Magistrate of Yongcheng under Jin, and the family lived at Linhuai for generations.

sentences.zh: 建生會，歷琅邪內史，從元帝度江，居丹楊。

translations.literal: Jian begot Hui, who served as Administrator of Langya; following Emperor Yuan he crossed the Yangzi and dwelt in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Hui held the post of Administrator of Langya; he followed Emperor Yuan across the Yangzi and settled in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 曾孫彥英，宋給事中、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: A great-grandson Yan Ying was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Regular Attendant of the General-in-Flexibility in Song.
translations.idiomatic: A great-grandson, Yan Ying, served Song as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Regular Attendant of the General-in-Flexibility.

sentences.zh: 二子：隱人、逸人。

translations.literal: Two sons: Yinren and Yiren.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yinren and Yiren.

sentences.zh: 梁末又徙晉陵。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang they moved again to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the end of Liang the family moved again to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 隱人五世孫子翼。

translations.literal: Yinren's fifth-generation descendant was Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yinren's fifth-generation descendant was Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 南陽劉氏出自長沙定王。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Nanyang derives from the King Ding of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanyang Liu trace their line to the King Ding of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 生安衆康侯丹，襲封三世，徙沮陽。

translations.literal: He begot Dan, Marquis Kang of Anzhong; the enfeoffment was inherited through three generations; they moved to Juyang.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant Dan, Marquis Kang of Anzhong, held the title for three generations before the line moved to Juyang.

sentences.zh: 裔孫廙字恭嗣，魏侍中、關內侯，無子，以弟子阜嗣。

translations.literal: A descendant Yi, styled Gongsi, was Palace Attendant and Marquis Within the Passes under Wei; having no son, his younger brother's son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: A later descendant, Yi, styled Gongsi, served Wei as Palace Attendant and Marquis Within the Passes; childless, he was succeeded by his nephew Fu.

sentences.zh: 阜字伯陵，陳留太守。

translations.literal: Fu, styled Bolin, was Governor of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, styled Bolin, served as Governor of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 生喬，字仲彥，晉太傅軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: He begot Qiao, styled Zhongyan, Army Adviser Sacrificer under the Grand Tutor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Qiao, styled Zhongyan, who served Jin as Army Adviser Sacrificer to the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 生挺，潁川太守。

translations.literal: He begot Ting, Governor of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's son Ting was Governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 二子：簡、耽。

translations.literal: Two sons: Jian and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Ting had two sons: Jian and Dan.

sentences.zh: 耽字敬道，為尚道令。

translations.literal: Dan, styled Jingdao, was Magistrate of Shangdao.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, styled Jingdao, served as Magistrate of Shangdao.

sentences.zh: 生柳，字叔惠，徐、兗、江三州刺史，又徙江陵。

translations.literal: He begot Liu, styled Shuhui, Governor of the three provinces Xu, Yan, and Jiang; he also moved to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's son Liu, styled Shuhui, served in turn as Governor of Xu, Yan, and Jiang, and the family later moved to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 曾孫虬。

translations.literal: A great-grandson was Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu's great-grandson was Qiu.

sentences.zh: 廣平劉氏出自漢景帝子趙敬肅王彭祖。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Guangping derives from Peng Zu, son of Emperor Jing of Han, King Jingsu of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangping Liu stem from King Jingsu of Zhao Peng Zu, son of Emperor Jing of Han.

sentences.zh: 彭祖生陰城思侯蒼，蒼薨，嗣子有罪不得立，遂居廣平肥鄉。

translations.literal: Peng Zu begot Cang, Marquis Si of Yincheng; when Cang died, the heir had guilt and could not be established, so they dwelt at Feixiang in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Zu had a son Cang, Marquis Si of Yincheng; when Cang died his intended heir was disqualified for crime, and the line settled at Feixiang in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 蒼十一世孫邵，字孔才，魏散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Cang's eleventh-generation descendant Shao, styled Kongcai, was Regular Attendant of the General-in-Flexibility under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cang's eleventh-generation descendant Shao, styled Kongcai, served Wei as Regular Attendant of the General-in-Flexibility.

sentences.zh: 十一世孫藻。

translations.literal: An eleventh-generation descendant was Zao.
translations.idiomatic: An eleventh-generation descendant was Zao.

sentences.zh: 丹楊劉氏，世居句容。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Danyang dwelt for generations at Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: The Danyang Liu lived at Jurong for generations.

sentences.zh: 曹州南華劉氏出自漢楚元王交之後，自彭城避地徙南華，築堌以居，世號「劉堌」。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Nanhua in Cao Prefecture derives from descendants of Jiao, King Yuan of Chu of Han; fleeing Pengcheng they moved to Nanhua, built a walled settlement to dwell, and for generations were called "Liugu."
translations.idiomatic: The Nanhua Liu of Cao Prefecture descend from King Yuan of Chu Jiao; they left Pengcheng for Nanhua, built a walled settlement there, and were known for generations as the "Liu Fortress" line.

sentences.zh: 隋有東萊令劉晉字進之。

translations.literal: Under Sui there was Liu Jin, styled Jinzhi, Magistrate of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui one Liu Jin, styled Jinzhi, served as Magistrate of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 三子：郁、多讓、多退。

translations.literal: Three sons: Yu, Duorang, and Duotui.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had three sons: Yu, Duorang, and Duotui.

sentences.zh: 劉氏定著七房：一曰彭城，二曰尉氏，三曰臨淮，四曰南陽，五曰廣平，六曰丹楊，七曰南華。

translations.literal: The Liu clan is definitively recorded in seven branches: first Pengcheng, second Weishi, third Linhuai, fourth Nanyang, fifth Guangping, sixth Danyang, seventh Nanhua.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu clan is recorded in seven established branches: Pengcheng, Weishi, Linhuai, Nanyang, Guangping, Danyang, and Nanhua.

sentences.zh: 宰相十二人。

translations.literal: Twelve chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 彭城房有滋、文靜、瞻；

translations.literal: The Pengcheng branch had Zi, Wenjing, and Zhan;
translations.idiomatic: The Pengcheng branch produced Zi, Wenjing, and Zhan;

sentences.zh: 尉氏房有仁軌、琢；

translations.literal: The Weishi branch had Rengui and Zhuo;
translations.idiomatic: The Weishi branch produced Rengui and Zhuo;

sentences.zh: 臨淮房有禕之；

translations.literal: The Linhuai branch had Yizhi;
translations.idiomatic: The Linhuai branch produced Yizhi;

sentences.zh: 南陽房有洎；

translations.literal: The Nanyang branch had Ji;
translations.idiomatic: The Nanyang branch produced Ji;

sentences.zh: 廣平房有祥道、景先、從一；

translations.literal: The Guangping branch had Xiangdao, Jingxian, and Congyi;
translations.idiomatic: The Guangping branch produced Xiangdao, Jingxian, and Congyi;

sentences.zh: 丹楊房有鄴；

translations.literal: The Danyang branch had Ye;
translations.idiomatic: The Danyang branch produced Ye;

sentences.zh: 南華房有晏。

translations.literal: The Nanhua branch had Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanhua branch produced Yan.

sentences.zh: 河南劉氏河南劉氏本出匈奴之族。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Henan—the Liu clan of Henan originally came from the Xiongnu race.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Liu—the Henan Liu line originally sprang from the Xiongnu people.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖以宗女妻冒頓，其俗貴者皆從母姓，因改為劉氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han gave a clan daughter in marriage to Modu; their custom was that the honored all took the mother's surname, therefore they changed to the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han married a clan princess to Modu; among the Xiongnu elite it was custom to take the mother's surname, and so the line became Liu.

sentences.zh: 左賢王去卑裔孫庫仁，字沒根，後魏南部大人、凌江將軍。

translations.literal: Left Wise King Qubei's descendant Kulun, styled Meigen, was Southern Tribal Chieftain of Later Wei and General Who Crosses the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Kulun, styled Meigen, a descendant of the Left Wise King Qubei, served Later Wei as Southern Tribal Chieftain and General Who Crosses the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 弟眷，生羅辰，定州刺史、永安敬公。

translations.literal: Younger brother Juan begot Luochen, Governor of Dingzhou and Duke Jing of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Kulun's younger brother Juan had a son Luochen, Governor of Dingzhou and Duke Jing of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 其後又居遼東襄平，徙河南。

translations.literal: Thereafter they again dwelt at Xiangping in Liaodong; they moved to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later the family settled at Xiangping in Liaodong before moving to Henan.

sentences.zh: 羅辰五世孫環雋，字仲賢，北齊中書侍郎、秀容懿公。

translations.literal: Luochen's fifth-generation descendant Huan Juan, styled Zhongxian, was Vice Director of the Secretariat of Northern Qi and Duke Yi of Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Luochen's fifth-generation descendant Huan Juan, styled Zhongxian, served Northern Qi as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed Duke Yi of Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 弟仕雋。

translations.literal: Younger brother Shijuan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Shijuan.

sentences.zh: 河南劉氏，宰相一人。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Henan: one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Henan Liu, one man served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 崇望。

translations.literal: Chongwang.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwang.

sentences.zh: 蕭蕭氏出自姬姓，帝嚳之後。

translations.literal: Xiao—the Xiao clan derives from the Ji surname; descendants of Emperor Ku.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao—the Xiao clan springs from the Ji surname and descends from Emperor Ku.

sentences.zh: 商帝乙庶子微子，周封為宋公，弟仲衍八世孫戴公生子衎，字樂父，裔孫大心平南宮長萬有功，封於蕭，以為附庸，今徐州蕭縣是也，子孫因以為氏。

translations.literal: The lesser son of Emperor Yi of Shang, Weizi, was enfeoffed by Zhou as Duke of Song; the eighth-generation descendant of his younger brother Zhongyan, Duke Dai, begot Zikang, styled Yuefu; a descendant Daxin pacified the merit of Nan Gongchang Wan; enfeoffed at Xiao as a vassal state—this is today's Xiao county in Xuzhou—descendants therefore took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Weizi, a lesser son of Emperor Yi of Shang, was enfeoffed by Zhou as Duke of Song. Duke Dai, eighth-generation descendant of Weizi's younger brother Zhongyan, had a son Zikang, styled Yuefu. A later descendant, Daxin, won credit for pacifying the rebellion of Wan Chang of the Southern Palace and was enfeoffed at Xiao as a dependent state—the present Xiao county in Xuzhou—after which the clan took Xiao as its surname.

sentences.zh: 其後楚滅蕭，裔孫不疑為楚相春申君上客，世居豐沛。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chu destroyed Xiao; a descendant Buyi was a chief guest of Lord Chunshen, Chancellor of Chu; they dwelt for generations at Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chu extinguished Xiao, a descendant Buyi became a leading retainer of Lord Chunshen, Chancellor of Chu, and the clan settled at Feng and Pei for generations.

sentences.zh: 漢有丞相酇文終侯何，二子：遺、則。

translations.literal: Under Han there was He, Marquis Wenzhong of Pei, Chancellor; two sons: Yi and Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, Xiao He, Chancellor and Marquis Wenzhong of Pei, had two sons: Yi and Ze.

sentences.zh: 則生彪，字伯文，諫議大夫、侍中，以事始徙蘭陵丞縣。

translations.literal: Ze begot Biao, styled Bowen, Grand Adviser and Palace Attendant; because of events he first moved to Chengxian in Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Ze's son Biao, styled Bowen, served as Grand Adviser and Palace Attendant; after certain events the family first moved to Chengxian in Lanling.

sentences.zh: 生章，公府掾。

translations.literal: He begot Zhang, an aide in the public offices.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had a son Zhang, who served as an aide in the public offices.

sentences.zh: 章生仰，字惠高，生晧。

translations.literal: Zhang begot Yang, styled Huigao, who begot Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's son Yang, styled Huigao, had a son Hao.

sentences.zh: 晧生望之，御史大夫，徙杜陵。

translations.literal: Hao begot Wangzhi, Censor-in-Chief; they moved to Duling.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's son Wangzhi served as Censor-in-Chief, and the family moved to Duling.

sentences.zh: 生育，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He begot Yu, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi's son Yu served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 生紹，御史中丞，復還蘭陵。

translations.literal: He begot Shao, Vice Censor-in-Chief; they returned again to Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had a son Shao, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and the family returned to Lanling.

sentences.zh: 生閎，光祿勳。

translations.literal: He begot Hong, Minister of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's son Hong served as Minister of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 閎生闡，濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Hong begot Chan, Governor of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Chan was Governor of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 闡生冰，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Chan begot Bing, Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chan's son Bing served as Governor of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 冰生苞，後漢中山相。

translations.literal: Bing begot Bao, Chancellor of Zhongshan under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's son Bao served Later Han as Chancellor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 生周，博士。

translations.literal: He begot Zhou, an Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had a son Zhou, who served as an Erudite.

sentences.zh: 周生蟜，虵丘長。

translations.literal: Zhou begot Jiao, Chief of Sheqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's son Jiao was Chief of Sheqiu.

sentences.zh: 蟜生逵，州從事。

translations.literal: Jiao begot Kui, a provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's son Kui served as a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 逵生休，孝廉。

translations.literal: Kui begot Xiu, a Filial and Incorrupt candidate.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's son Xiu was a Filial and Incorrupt candidate.

sentences.zh: 休生豹，廣陵郡丞。

translations.literal: Xiu begot Bao, Assistant Administrator of Guangling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's son Bao served as Assistant Administrator of Guangling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 豹生裔，太中大夫。

translations.literal: Bao begot Yi, Grand Master of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son Yi served as Grand Master of Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 生整，字公齊，晉淮南令，過江居南蘭陵武進之東城里。

translations.literal: He begot Zheng, styled Gongqi, Magistrate of Huainan under Jin; crossing the Yangzi he dwelt in Dongchengli of Wujin in Southern Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had a son Zheng, styled Gongqi, who served Jin as Magistrate of Huainan; after crossing the Yangzi the family settled in Dongchengli of Wujin in Southern Lanling.

sentences.zh: 三子：儁、鎋、烈。

translations.literal: Three sons: Jun, Xiang, and Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had three sons: Jun, Xiang, and Lie.

sentences.zh: 苞九世孫卓，字子略，洮陽令，女為宋高祖繼母，號皇舅房。

translations.literal: Bao's ninth-generation descendant Zhuo, styled Zilue, was Magistrate of Taoyang; his daughter was the stepmother of the Founding Emperor of Song, and the line was styled the Imperial Uncle Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's ninth-generation descendant Zhuo, styled Zilue, was Magistrate of Taoyang; his daughter became stepmother to the Founding Emperor of Song, and the line was called the Imperial Uncle Branch.

sentences.zh: 卓生源之，字君流，徐兗二州刺史，襲封陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Zhuo begot Yuanzhi, styled Junliu, Governor of the two provinces Xu and Yan; he inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Yang county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's son Yuanzhi, styled Junliu, served as Governor of Xu and Yan and inherited the title Marquis of Yang county.

sentences.zh: 生思話，郢州都督，封陽穆侯。

translations.literal: He begot Sihua, Area Commander of Yingzhou; enfeoffed as Marquis Mu of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi's son Sihua served as Area Commander of Yingzhou and was enfeoffed Marquis Mu of Yang.

sentences.zh: 六子：惠開、惠明、惠基、惠休、惠朗、惠蒨。

translations.literal: Six sons: Huikai, Huiming, Huiji, Huixiu, Huilang, and Huiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua had six sons: Huikai, Huiming, Huiji, Huixiu, Huilang, and Huiqian.

sentences.zh: 惠蒨，齊左戶尚書。

translations.literal: Huiqian was Minister of the Left Household under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqian served Qi as Minister of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 生介。

translations.literal: He begot Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqian had a son Jie.

sentences.zh: 齊梁房：整第二子鎋，濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Qi-Liang Branch: Zheng's second son Xiang, Governor of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Qi-Liang Branch: Zheng's second son Xiang served as Governor of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 生副子，州治中從事。

translations.literal: He begot Fuzi, a provincial chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had a son Fuzi, who served as a provincial chief aide.

sentences.zh: 生道賜，宋南臺治中侍御史。

translations.literal: He begot Daoci, Attending Censor and Chief Aide of the Southern Office under Song.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzi's son Daoci served Song as Attending Censor and Chief Aide of the Southern Office.

sentences.zh: 三子：尚之、順之、崇之。

translations.literal: Three sons: Shangzhi, Shunzhi, and Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Daoci had three sons: Shangzhi, Shunzhi, and Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 順之字文緯，齊丹楊尹、臨湘懿侯。

translations.literal: Shunzhi, styled Wenwei, was Prefect of Danyang under Qi and Marquis Yi of Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi, styled Wenwei, served Qi as Prefect of Danyang and was enfeoffed Marquis Yi of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 十子：懿、敷、衍、暢、融、宏、偉、秀、憺、恢。

translations.literal: Ten sons: Yi, Fu, Yan, Chang, Rong, Hong, Wei, Xiu, Dan, and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi had ten sons: Yi, Fu, Yan, Chang, Rong, Hong, Wei, Xiu, Dan, and Hui.

sentences.zh: 衍，梁高祖武皇帝也，號齊梁房。

translations.literal: Yan was the Founding Martial Emperor of Liang, also called the Qi-Liang Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Emperor Wu, founding emperor of Liang, and the line is called the Qi-Liang Branch.

sentences.zh: 懿字元達，長沙宣武王。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Yuanda, was King Xuanwu of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Yuanda, was King Xuanwu of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 七子：業、藻、象、猷、朗、軌、明。

translations.literal: Seven sons: Ye, Zao, Xiang, You, Lang, Gui, and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had seven sons: Ye, Zao, Xiang, You, Lang, Gui, and Ming.

sentences.zh: 明字靖通，梁貞陽侯，曾孫文憬。

translations.literal: Ming, styled Jingtong, was Marquis Zhenyang of Liang; a great-grandson was Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Ming, styled Jingtong, was Marquis Zhenyang of Liang; his great-grandson was Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 梁高祖武皇帝八子：統、綱、續、繹、綜、績、綸、紀。

translations.literal: The Founding Martial Emperor of Liang had eight sons: Tong, Gang, Xu, Yi, Zong, Ji, Lun, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang had eight sons: Tong, Gang, Xu, Yi, Zong, Ji, Lun, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 統，昭明太子。

translations.literal: Tong was Crown Prince Zhaoming.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was Crown Prince Zhaoming.

sentences.zh: 綱，簡文皇帝也。

translations.literal: Gang was Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Gang became Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 統五子：歡、譽、詧、𧫣、譼。

translations.literal: Tong's five sons: Huan, Yu, Cha, Liao, and Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had five sons: Huan, Yu, Cha, Liao, and Tan.

sentences.zh: 蕭氏定著二房；

translations.literal: The Xiao clan is definitively recorded in two branches;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao clan is recorded in two established branches;

sentences.zh: 一曰皇舅房，二曰齊梁房。

translations.literal: first the Imperial Uncle Branch, second the Qi-Liang Branch.
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Uncle Branch and the Qi-Liang Branch.

sentences.zh: 宰相十人。

translations.literal: Ten chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Ten men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 皇舅房有至忠；

translations.literal: The Imperial Uncle Branch had Zhizhong;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Uncle Branch produced Zhizhong;

sentences.zh: 齊梁房有鄴、嵩、華、俛、倣、復、寘、遘、瑀。

translations.literal: The Qi-Liang Branch had Ye, Song, Hua, Fu, Fang, Fu, Zhi, Gou, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi-Liang Branch produced Ye, Song, Hua, Fu, Fang, Fu, Zhi, Gou, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 竇竇氏出自姒姓，夏后氏帝相失國，其妃有仍氏女方娠，逃出自竇，奔歸有仍氏，生子曰少康。

translations.literal: Dou—the Dou clan derives from the Si surname; Emperor Xiang of the Xia lost the state; his consort, a woman of the Youreng clan, was pregnant; fleeing she emerged from Dou, ran back to the Youreng clan, and bore a son called Shaokang.
translations.idiomatic: Dou—the Dou clan springs from the Si surname. When Emperor Xiang of Xia lost his throne, his consort, a woman of the Youreng clan, was pregnant; she fled through Dou Pass, returned to Youreng, and bore a son named Shaokang.

sentences.zh: 少康二子：曰杼，曰龍，留居有仍，遂為竇氏。

translations.literal: Shaokang's two sons: one called Zhu, one called Long; remaining to dwell at Youreng, they thus became the Dou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shaokang had two sons, Zhu and Long; those who remained at Youreng became the Dou clan.

sentences.zh: 龍六十九世孫鳴犢，為晉大夫，葬常山。

translations.literal: Long's sixty-ninth-generation descendant Mingdu was a grandee of Jin; he was buried at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Long's sixty-ninth-generation descendant Mingdu was a grandee of Jin and was buried at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 及六卿分晉，竇氏遂居平陽。

translations.literal: When the Six Ministers divided Jin, the Dou clan then dwelt at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Ministers partitioned Jin, the Dou clan settled at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 鳴犢生仲，仲生臨，臨生亶，亶生陽，陽生庚，庚生誦，二子：世、扈。

translations.literal: Mingdu begot Zhong; Zhong begot Lin; Lin begot Dan; Dan begot Yang; Yang begot Geng; Geng begot Song; two sons: Shi and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdu's line ran through Zhong, Lin, Dan, Yang, and Geng to Song, who had two sons: Shi and Hu.

sentences.zh: 世生嬰，漢丞相魏其侯也。

translations.literal: Shi begot Ying, Chancellor and Marquis of Weiji under Han.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's son Ying was Dou Ying, Chancellor and Marquis of Weiji under Han.

sentences.zh: 扈二子：經、充。

translations.literal: Hu's two sons: Jing and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had two sons: Jing and Chong.

sentences.zh: 經，秦大將軍，生甫，漢孝文皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Jing, a great general of Qin, begot Fu, elder brother of the Empress Xiaowen of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, a great general of Qin, had a son Fu, elder brother of Empress Xiaowen of Han.

sentences.zh: 充，避秦之難，徙居清河，漢贈安成侯，葬觀津。

translations.literal: Chong, avoiding the troubles of Qin, moved to dwell at Qinghe; Han posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Ancheng; he was buried at Guanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Chong fled the turmoil of Qin and moved to Qinghe; Han posthumously enfeoffed him Marquis of Ancheng, and he was buried at Guanjin.

sentences.zh: 二子：長君、廣國。

translations.literal: Two sons: Changjun and Guangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Changjun and Guangguo.

sentences.zh: 廣國字少君，章武景侯。

translations.literal: Guangguo, styled Shaojun, was Marquis Jing of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangguo, styled Shaojun, held the title Marquis Jing of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 二子：定、誼。

translations.literal: Two sons: Ding and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangguo had two sons: Ding and Yi.

sentences.zh: 誼生賞，襲章武侯，宣帝時，以吏二千石徙扶風平陵。

translations.literal: Yi begot Shang, who inherited Marquis Wu of Zhangwu; in the time of Emperor Xuan, as an official of the two-thousand-dan rank he moved to Pingling in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Shang inherited the title Marquis Wu of Zhangwu; under Emperor Xuan he was transferred to Pingling in Fufeng as an official of the two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 二子：壽、邕。

translations.literal: Two sons: Shou and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang had two sons: Shou and Yong.

sentences.zh: 壽，護羌校尉，燉煌南竇祖也。

translations.literal: Shou was Protector-General of the Qiang; he was the southern Dou ancestor at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Shou served as Protector-General of the Qiang and became the southern Dou ancestor at Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 邕，南陽太守，生猛，定安太守。

translations.literal: Yong was Governor of Nanyang; he begot Meng, Governor of Ding'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yong served as Governor of Nanyang; his son Meng was Governor of Ding'an.

sentences.zh: 二子：秀、敷。

translations.literal: Two sons: Xiu and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng had two sons: Xiu and Fu.

sentences.zh: 秀二子：丕、林。

translations.literal: Xiu's two sons: Pi and Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had two sons: Pi and Lin.

sentences.zh: 林，後漢武威太守、太中大夫，避難徙居武威，為武威竇祖。

translations.literal: Lin was Governor of Wuwei and Grand Master of Palace Affairs under Later Han; fleeing troubles he moved to dwell at Wuwei and became the Wuwei Dou ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Lin served Later Han as Governor of Wuwei and Grand Master of Palace Affairs; fleeing turmoil he settled in Wuwei and became the Wuwei Dou ancestor.

sentences.zh: 敷三子：平年、友、融。

translations.literal: Fu's three sons: Pingnian, You, and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had three sons: Pingnian, You, and Rong.

sentences.zh: 融字周公，大司馬、安豐戴侯。

translations.literal: Rong, styled Gongzhou, was Grand Marshal and Marquis Dai of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, styled Gongzhou, served as Grand Marshal and was enfeoffed Marquis Dai of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 生穆，城門校尉、駙馬都尉，襲安豐侯。

translations.literal: He begot Mu, Colonel of the City Gates and Commandant of Feathered Riders; he inherited Marquis of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's son Mu served as Colonel of the City Gates and Commandant of Feathered Riders and inherited the title Marquis of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 五子：勳、宣、襃、霸、嘉。

translations.literal: Five sons: Xun, Xuan, Bao, Ba, and Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Mu had five sons: Xun, Xuan, Bao, Ba, and Jia.

sentences.zh: 宣生尚，以家難隨母徙隴右，為隴右竇祖。

translations.literal: Xuan begot Shang; because of family troubles he followed his mother and moved to Longyou, becoming the Longyou Dou ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's son Shang, caught up in a family crisis, followed his mother to Longyou and became the Dou ancestor of that region.

sentences.zh: 嘉，少府兼侍中、安豐侯。

translations.literal: Jia was Chamberlain for the National Treasury and concurrently Palace Attendant, Marquis of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jia served as Chamberlain for the National Treasury and concurrently Palace Attendant, and held the title Marquis of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 三子：潛、奉、萬全。

translations.literal: Three sons: Qian, Feng, and Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia had three sons: Qian, Feng, and Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 奉子武，特進槐里侯，晉贈文嘉貞侯。

translations.literal: Feng's son Wu was Special Advance and Marquis of Huaili; Jin posthumously enfeoffed him Marquis Zhen of Wenjia.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's son Wu rose to Special Advance and Marquis of Huaili; Jin posthumously enfeoffed him Marquis Zhen of Wenjia.

sentences.zh: 萬全襲安豐侯。

translations.literal: Wanquan inherited Marquis of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wanquan inherited the title Marquis of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 二子：會宗、章。

translations.literal: Two sons: Huizong and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wanquan had two sons: Huizong and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 會宗子孫居武功扶風。

translations.literal: Huizong's descendants dwelt at Wugong in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong's descendants settled at Wugong in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 章，大鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Zhang was Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang served as Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 三子：陶、唐、統。

translations.literal: Three sons: Tao, Tang, and Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had three sons: Tao, Tang, and Tong.

sentences.zh: 統字敬道，鴈門太守，以竇武之難，亡入鮮卑拓拔部，使居南境代郡平城，以間窺中國，號沒鹿回部落大人。

translations.literal: Tong, styled Jingdao, was Governor of Yanmen; because of the Dou Wu affair he fled into the Tuoba Xianbei tribe, was made to dwell on the southern frontier at Pingcheng in Dai Commandery, to spy on China from afar, and was styled Grand Chieftain of the Moluhui tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, styled Jingdao, was Governor of Yanmen; after the catastrophe of Dou Wu he fled to the Tuoba Xianbei and was settled on the southern frontier at Pingcheng in Dai Commandery, from which he watched the Central Realm and was styled Grand Chieftain of the Moluhui tribe.

sentences.zh: 後得匈奴舊境，又徙居之。

translations.literal: Later he gained the old territory of the Xiongnu and moved to dwell there again.
translations.idiomatic: Later he gained the Xiongnu's former territory and moved the tribe there.

sentences.zh: 生賓，字力延，襲部落大人。

translations.literal: He begot Bin, styled Liyan, who inherited the tribal chieftaincy.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had a son Bin, styled Liyan, who inherited leadership of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 二子：異、他。

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Ta.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had two sons: Yi and Ta.

sentences.zh: 他字建侯，亦襲部落大人，為後魏神元皇帝所殺，併其部落。

translations.literal: Ta, styled Jianhou, also inherited the tribal chieftaincy; he was killed by Emperor Shenyuan of Later Wei, who annexed his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Ta, styled Jianhou, also inherited the chieftaincy; Later Wei's Emperor Shenyuan killed him and absorbed his tribe.

sentences.zh: 他生勤，字羽德，穆帝復使領舊部落，命為紇豆陵氏。

translations.literal: Ta begot Qin, styled Yude; Emperor Mu again had him lead the old tribe and commanded them to take the name Heldouling clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ta's son Qin, styled Yude, was again placed over the old tribe by Emperor Mu, who ordered the clan to adopt the surname Heldouling.

sentences.zh: 晉冊為穆帝為代王，亦封勤忠義侯，徙居五原。

translations.literal: When Jin enfeoffed Emperor Mu as King of Dai, [Qin] was also enfeoffed Marquis of Zhongyi, and [the clan] moved to dwell at Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin enfeoffed Emperor Mu as King of Dai, Qin was also enfeoffed Marquis of Loyalty and Righteousness, and the clan moved to Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 生子真，字玄道，率衆入魏，為征西大將軍。

translations.literal: He begot Zizhen, styled Xuandao, who led the multitude into Wei and became General-in-Chief Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had a son Zizhen, styled Xuandao, who led his following into Wei and rose to General-in-Chief Who Conquers the West.

sentences.zh: 生朗，字明遠，復領父衆。

translations.literal: He begot Lang, styled Mingyuan, who again led his father's multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen's son Lang, styled Mingyuan, again took command of his father's following.

sentences.zh: 二子：滔、祐。

translations.literal: Two sons: Tao and You.
translations.idiomatic: Lang had two sons: Tao and You.

sentences.zh: 祐，遼東公，亦領部落。

translations.literal: You was Duke of Liaodong and also led the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: You held the title Duke of Liaodong and also led the tribal following.

sentences.zh: 三子：提、拓、巖。

translations.literal: Three sons: Ti, Tuo, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: You had three sons: Ti, Tuo, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 自拓不領部落，為魏侍中、遼東宣王。

translations.literal: From Tuo onward [the line] no longer led the tribe; he was Palace Attendant under Wei and King Xuan of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: From Tuo onward the line no longer led the tribe; Tuo served Wei as Palace Attendant and was enfeoffed King Xuan of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 巖，安西大將軍、遼東穆公，從孝武徙洛陽，自是遂為河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Yan was General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the West and Duke Mu of Liaodong; following Emperor Xiaowu he moved to Luoyang, and from this time forth they became people of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan served as General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the West and was enfeoffed Duke Mu of Liaodong; he followed Emperor Xiaowu to Luoyang, and from then on the clan were natives of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 三子：那、敦、略。

translations.literal: Three sons: Na, Dun, and Lue.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had three sons: Na, Dun, and Lue.

sentences.zh: 略字六頭，征北大將軍、建昌孝公。

translations.literal: Lue, styled Liutou, was General-in-Chief Who Conquers the North and Duke Xiao of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lue, styled Liutou, rose to General-in-Chief Who Conquers the North and was enfeoffed Duke Xiao of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 孝文帝之世，復為竇氏。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, [the clan] again became the Dou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen the clan resumed the surname Dou.

sentences.zh: 五子：興、拔、岳、善、熾。

translations.literal: Five sons: Xing, Ba, Yue, Shan, and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Lue had five sons: Xing, Ba, Yue, Shan, and Chi.

sentences.zh: 岳，後周清河廣平二郡太守、神武郡公，與善、熾子孫號為「三祖」。

translations.literal: Yue was Governor of the two commanderies Qinghe and Guangping under Later Zhou and Duke of Shenwu Commandery; the descendants of Shan and Chi together with his were styled the "Three Ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Yue served Later Zhou as Governor of Qinghe and Guangping and was enfeoffed Duke of Shenwu Commandery; his line, together with the descendants of Shan and Chi, was known as the "Three Ancestors."

sentences.zh: 岳二子：甝、毅。

translations.literal: Yue's two sons: Lin and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had two sons: Lin and Yi.

sentences.zh: 善一名溫，西魏汾華隴三州刺史、永富縣男。

translations.literal: Shan, also named Wen, was Governor of the three provinces Fen, Hua, and Long under Western Wei and Baron of Yongfu county.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, also called Wen, served Western Wei as Governor of Fen, Hua, and Long and was enfeoffed Baron of Yongfu county.

sentences.zh: 生榮定。

translations.literal: He begot Rongding.
translations.idiomatic: Shan had a son Rongding.

sentences.zh: 熾，周太保、鄧公。

translations.literal: Chi was Grand Mentor under Zhou and Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Chi served Zhou as Grand Mentor and was enfeoffed Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 六子：恭、覽、深、嶷、誼、威。

translations.literal: Six sons: Gong, Lan, Shen, Ni, Yi, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chi had six sons: Gong, Lan, Shen, Ni, Yi, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 竇武之後又有敬遠，封西河公，居扶風平陵，孫善衡。

translations.literal: Among the descendants of Dou Wu there was also Jingyuan, enfeoffed Duke of Xihe, who dwelt at Pingling in Fufeng; his grandson was Shanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu's line also produced Jingyuan, enfeoffed Duke of Xihe, who settled at Pingling in Fufeng; his grandson was Shanheng.

sentences.zh: 竇氏定著二房：一曰三祖房，二曰平陵房。

translations.literal: The Dou clan is definitively recorded in two branches: first the Three Ancestors Branch, second the Pingling Branch.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou clan is recorded in two established branches: the Three Ancestors Branch and the Pingling Branch.

sentences.zh: 宰相六人。

translations.literal: Six chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Six men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 三祖房有德玄、懷貞、抗、參、威；

translations.literal: The Three Ancestors Branch had Dexuan, Huaizhen, Kang, Can, and Wei;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Ancestors Branch produced Dexuan, Huaizhen, Kang, Can, and Wei;

sentences.zh: 平陵房有易直。

translations.literal: the Pingling Branch had Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: the Pingling Branch produced Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 陳陳氏出自媯姓，虞帝舜之後。

translations.literal: The Chen clan derives from the Gui surname, being descendants of Emperor Shun of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen clan traces its line to the Gui surname and descends from Emperor Shun of Yu.

sentences.zh: 夏禹封舜子商均於虞城，三十二世孫遏父為周陶正，武王妻以元女大姬，生滿，封之於陳，賜姓媯，以奉舜祀，是為胡公。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia enfeoffed Shun's son Shangjun at Yucheng; a thirty-second-generation descendant Efu served Zhou as Director of Pottery; King Wu gave him in marriage his eldest daughter Da Ji, who bore Man; he was enfeoffed at Chen, granted the surname Gui, to maintain Shun's sacrifices — this was Duke Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia enfeoffed Shun's son Shangjun at Yucheng; thirty-two generations later Efu served Zhou as Director of Pottery; King Wu married him to his eldest daughter Da Ji, and their son Man was enfeoffed at Chen with the surname Gui to maintain Shun's sacrifices — Duke Hu.

sentences.zh: 九世孫厲公他生敬仲完，奔齊，以國為姓。

translations.literal: A ninth-generation descendant, Duke Li Ta, begot Jingzhong Wan, who fled to Qi and took the state name as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations later Duke Li Ta had a son Jingzhong Wan, who fled to Qi and took Chen as his surname.

sentences.zh: 既而食邑於田，又為田氏。

translations.literal: Thereafter receiving a fief at Tian, [the line] also became the Tian clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later granted a fief at Tian, the line also became known as the Tian clan.

sentences.zh: 十五世孫齊王建為秦所滅。

translations.literal: A fifteenth-generation descendant Jian, King of Qi, was destroyed by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen generations later Jian, King of Qi, was overthrown by Qin.

sentences.zh: 三子：昇、桓、軫。

translations.literal: Three sons: Sheng, Huan, and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had three sons: Sheng, Huan, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 桓稱王氏。

translations.literal: Huan took the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan adopted the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 軫，楚相，封潁川侯，因徙潁川，稱陳氏。

translations.literal: Zhen was Chancellor of Chu, enfeoffed Marquis of Yingchuan; he therefore moved to Yingchuan and took the surname Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen served Chu as chancellor, was enfeoffed Marquis of Yingchuan, moved there, and took the surname Chen.

sentences.zh: 生嬰，秦東陽令史。

translations.literal: He begot Ying, a clerk of Dongyang under Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had a son Ying, who served Qin as a clerk of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 嬰生成安君餘，餘生軌，軌生審，審生安，安生恒，恒生願，願四子：清、察、齊、尚。

translations.literal: Ying begot Chenganjun Yu; Yu begot Gui; Gui begot Shen; Shen begot An; An begot Heng; Heng begot Yuan; Yuan's four sons: Qing, Cha, Qi, and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's line ran through Chenganjun Yu, Gui, Shen, An, and Heng to Yuan, who had four sons: Qing, Cha, Qi, and Shang.

sentences.zh: 齊生源，源三子：寔、崱、邃。

translations.literal: Qi begot Yuan; Yuan's three sons: Shi, Ce, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had a son Yuan, whose three sons were Shi, Ce, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 寔字仲弓，後漢大將軍掾屬，文範先生。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Zhonggong, was an aide under the Grand General of Later Han and was styled Master Wenfan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Zhonggong, served Later Han as an aide to the Grand General and was known as Master Wenfan.

sentences.zh: 六子：紀、夔、洽、諶、休、光。

translations.literal: Six sons: Ji, Kui, Qia, Chen, Xiu, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had six sons: Ji, Kui, Qia, Chen, Xiu, and Guang.

sentences.zh: 諶字季方，獻文先生。

translations.literal: Chen, styled Jifang, was styled Master Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Jifang, was known as Master Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 生青州刺史忠。

translations.literal: He begot Zhong, Governor of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had a son Zhong, who served as Governor of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 二子：佐、和。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zuo and He.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong had two sons: Zuo and He.

sentences.zh: 佐二子：準、徽。

translations.literal: Zuo's two sons: Zhun and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo had two sons: Zhun and Hui.

sentences.zh: 準字道基，晉太尉、廣陵元公。

translations.literal: Zhun, styled Daoji, was Grand Commandant under Jin and Duke Yuan of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun, styled Daoji, served Jin as Grand Commandant and was enfeoffed Duke Yuan of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 生伯眕，建興中度江居曲阿新豐湖。

translations.literal: He begot Bozhen, who in the Jianxing era crossed the Yangzi and dwelt at Xinfeng Lake in Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun's son Bozhen crossed the Yangzi during the Jianxing era and settled at Xinfeng Lake in Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 生匡，二子：赤松、世達。

translations.literal: He begot Kuang; two sons: Chisong and Shida.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen had a son Kuang, who had two sons: Chisong and Shida.

sentences.zh: 世達，長城令，徙居長城下若里，生丞相掾康。

translations.literal: Shida was Magistrate of Changcheng; he moved to dwell at Ruoli below Changcheng and begot Kang, an aide to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shida served as Magistrate of Changcheng, moved to Ruoli below Changcheng, and had a son Kang, who served as an aide to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 康生盱眙太守英，英生尚書郎公弼，公弼生步兵校尉鼎，鼎生散騎侍郎高，高生懷安令詠，詠生安成太守猛，猛生太常卿道巨，道巨生文讚。

translations.literal: Kang begot Ying, Governor of Xuyi; Ying begot Gongbi, Lang of the Masters of Writing; Gongbi begot Ding, Colonel of the Footsoldiers; Ding begot Gao, Gentleman Attendant of the General-in-Flexibility; Gao begot Yong, Magistrate of Huai'an; Yong begot Meng, Governor of Ancheng; Meng begot Daoju, Minister of Ceremonies; Daoju begot Wenzan.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's line ran through Ying, Governor of Xuyi; Gongbi, a Master of Writing; Ding, Colonel of the Footsoldiers; Gao, Gentleman Attendant of the General-in-Flexibility; Yong, Magistrate of Huai'an; Meng, Governor of Ancheng; and Daoju, Minister of Ceremonies, down to Wenzan.

sentences.zh: 文讚三子：談先、霸先、休先。

translations.literal: Wenzan's three sons: Tanxian, Baxian, and Xiuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzan had three sons: Tanxian, Baxian, and Xiuxian.

sentences.zh: 又有潁川陳忠，不知所承。

translations.literal: There was also Chen Zhong of Yingchuan, whose line of descent is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Chen Zhong of Yingchuan, but from whom he descended is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 陳氏宰相三人。

translations.literal: Three chancellors of the Chen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Three men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 叔達、希烈、夷行。

translations.literal: Shuda, Xilie, and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuda, Xilie, and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 封封氏出自姜姓，炎帝裔孫鉅為黃帝師，胙土命氏，至夏后氏之世，封父列為諸侯，其地汴州封丘有封父亭，即封父所都。

translations.literal: The Feng clan derives from the Jiang surname; a descendant of Emperor Yan named Ju was teacher to the Yellow Emperor, and enfeoffment with land gave the clan its name; in the age of the Xia rulers Fengfu Lie was enfeoffed as a feudal lord; at Fengfu Pavilion in Fengqiu, Bian prefecture, lay the seat of Fengfu.
translations.idiomatic: The Feng clan traces its line to the Jiang surname; Ju, a descendant of Emperor Yan, was teacher to the Yellow Emperor, and the clan took its name from an enfeoffment; under Xia, Fengfu Lie was made a feudal lord, and Fengfu Pavilion in Fengqiu, Bian prefecture, marked his seat.

sentences.zh: 至周失國，子孫為齊大夫，遂居渤海蓨縣。

translations.literal: When Zhou lost the state, the descendants became great officers of Qi and then dwelt at Tiao county in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: After the line lost its state under Zhou, its descendants served Qi as great officers and settled at Tiao county in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 裔孫岌，字仲山，後漢侍中、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: A descendant Ji, styled Zhongshan, was Palace Attendant and Governor of Liang province under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: A later descendant, Ji, styled Zhongshan, served Later Han as Palace Attendant and Governor of Liang province.

sentences.zh: 生咺，咺四世孫仁，仁孫釋，晉侍中、東夷校尉。

translations.literal: He begot Xuan; Xuan's fourth-generation descendant was Ren; Ren's grandson was Shi, Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Eastern Yi under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had a son Xuan; four generations later came Ren, whose grandson Shi served Jin as Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 二子：、悛。

translations.literal: Two sons: [name lost in the text] and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had two sons; the name of the first is lost in the text, the second was Quan.

sentences.zh: 悛二子：放、弈。

translations.literal: Quan's two sons: Fang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan had two sons: Fang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 弈，燕太尉。

translations.literal: Yi was Grand Commandant of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served Yan as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 二子：蘄、勸。

translations.literal: Two sons: Qi and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had two sons: Qi and Quan.

sentences.zh: 蘄孫鑒，後魏滄水太守。

translations.literal: Qi's grandson was Jian, Governor of Cangshui under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's grandson Jian served Later Wei as Governor of Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 三子：琳、回、滑。

translations.literal: Three sons: Lin, Hui, and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had three sons: Lin, Hui, and Hua.

sentences.zh: 封氏宰相一人。

translations.literal: One chancellor of the Feng clan.
translations.idiomatic: One man of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 倫。

translations.literal: Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Lun.

sentences.zh: 楊楊氏出自姬姓，周宣王子尚父封為楊侯。

translations.literal: The Yang clan derives from the Ji surname; Shangfu, son of King Xuan of Zhou, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan traces its line to the Ji surname; Shangfu, son of King Xuan of Zhou, was enfeoffed Marquis of Yang.

sentences.zh: 一云晉武公子伯僑生文，文生突，羊舌大夫也。

translations.literal: One account says that Boqiao, son of the Duke Wu of Jin, begot Wen; Wen begot Tu, the Master of the Yangshe clan.
translations.idiomatic: One account holds that Boqiao, son of Duke Wu of Jin, had a son Wen, whose son Tu was the Master of the Yangshe clan.

sentences.zh: 又云晉之公族食邑於羊舌，凡三縣：一曰銅鞮，二曰楊氏，三曰平陽。

translations.literal: Another account says that the ducal house of Jin held fiefs at Yangshe, three counties in all: first Tongdi, second Yangshi, third Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Another account says the Jin ducal house held fiefs at Yangshe in three counties: Tongdi, Yangshi, and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 突生職，職五子：赤、肸、鮒、虎、季夙。

translations.literal: Tu begot Zhi; Zhi's five sons: Chi, Xi, Fu, Hu, and Jisu.
translations.idiomatic: Tu's son Zhi had five sons: Chi, Xi, Fu, Hu, and Jisu.

sentences.zh: 赤字伯華，為銅鞮大夫，生子容。

translations.literal: Chi, styled Bohua, was Grand Master of Tongdi; he begot Zirong.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, styled Bohua, served as Grand Master of Tongdi and had a son Zirong.

sentences.zh: 肸字叔向，亦曰叔譽。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Shuxiang, was also called Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, styled Shuxiang, was also known as Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 鮒字叔魚。

translations.literal: Fu, styled Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was styled Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 虎字叔羆，號羊舌四族。

translations.literal: Hu, styled Shupi, styled the Four Yangshe Clans.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, styled Shupi, gave his name to the Four Yangshe Clans.

sentences.zh: 叔向，晉太傅，食采楊氏，其地平陽楊氏縣是也。

translations.literal: Shuxiang was Grand Tutor of Jin; his fief was at Yangshi, the land being Yangshi county in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxiang served Jin as Grand Tutor; his fief was at Yangshi, in what is Yangshi county, Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 叔向生伯石，字食我，以邑為氏，號曰楊石，黨於祁盈，盈得罪於晉，幷滅羊舌氏，叔向子孫逃于華山仙谷，遂居華陰。

translations.literal: Shuxiang begot Boshi, styled Shiwuo, who took the fief as his surname and was styled Yang Shi; he allied with Qi Ying; when Ying offended Jin and the Yangshe clan was exterminated together with him, Shuxiang's descendants fled to Xiangu in Mount Hua and then dwelt at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxiang's son Boshi, styled Shiwuo, took his fief as surname and was called Yang Shi; he sided with Qi Ying, and when Ying brought ruin on himself and Jin exterminated the Yangshe clan as well, Shuxiang's descendants fled to Xiangu on Mount Hua and settled at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 有楊章者，生苞、朗、款。

translations.literal: There was one Yang Zhang, who begot Bao, Lang, and Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Yang Zhang, who had sons Bao, Lang, and Kuan.

sentences.zh: 苞為韓襄王將，守脩武，子孫因居河內。

translations.literal: Bao was a general for King Xiang of Han, guarding Xiuwu; his descendants therefore dwelt in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Bao served King Xiang of Han as a general and held Xiuwu; his descendants then settled in Henei.

sentences.zh: 朗為秦將，封臨晉君，子孫因居馮翊。

translations.literal: Lang was a Qin general, enfeoffed as Lord of Linjin; his descendants therefore dwelt in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lang served Qin as a general and was enfeoffed Lord of Linjin; his descendants then settled in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 款為秦上卿，生碩，字太初，從沛公征伐，為太史。

translations.literal: Kuan was Senior Minister of Qin; he begot Shuo, styled Taichu, who followed the Duke of Pei in campaigns and served as Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan served Qin as Senior Minister; his son Shuo, styled Taichu, joined the Duke of Pei's campaigns and became Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 八子：鷃、奮、甝、儵、熊、喜、鸇、魋。

translations.literal: Eight sons: Yan, Fen, Huan, Shu, Xiong, Xi, Guan, and Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Eight sons: Yan, Fen, Huan, Shu, Xiong, Xi, Guan, and Mei.

sentences.zh: 喜字幼羅，漢赤泉嚴侯。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Youruo, was Marquis Yan of Chiquan under Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, styled Youruo, was enfeoffed under Han as Marquis Yan of Chiquan.

sentences.zh: 生敷，字伯宗，赤泉定侯。

translations.literal: He begot Fu, styled Bozong, Marquis Ding of Chiquan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Fu, styled Bozong, Marquis Ding of Chiquan.

sentences.zh: 生胤，字毋害。

translations.literal: He begot Yin, styled Wuhai.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yin, styled Wuhai.

sentences.zh: 胤生敞，字君平，丞相、安平敬侯。

translations.literal: Yin begot Chang, styled Junping, Chancellor and Marquis Jing of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Chang, styled Junping, served as Chancellor and was enfeoffed Marquis Jing of Anping.

sentences.zh: 二子：忠、惲。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhong and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Zhong and Yun.

sentences.zh: 忠，安平頃侯。

translations.literal: Zhong was Marquis Qing of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was enfeoffed Marquis Qing of Anping.

sentences.zh: 生譚，屬國、安平侯。

translations.literal: He begot Tan, Chief of Dependent States and Marquis of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Tan, who served as Chief of Dependent States and was Marquis of Anping.

sentences.zh: 二子：寶、並。

translations.literal: Two sons: Bao and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Bao and Bing.

sentences.zh: 寶字稚淵。

translations.literal: Bao was styled Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was styled Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 二子：震、衡。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhen and Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Zhen and Heng.

sentences.zh: 震字伯起，太尉。

translations.literal: Zhen, styled Boqi, was Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, styled Boqi, served as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 五子：牧、里、秉、讓、奉。

translations.literal: Five sons: Mu, Li, Bing, Rang, and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons: Mu, Li, Bing, Rang, and Feng.

sentences.zh: 牧字孟信，荊州刺史、富波侯。

translations.literal: Mu, styled Mengxin, was Governor of Jing province and Marquis of Fubo.
translations.idiomatic: Mu, styled Mengxin, served as Governor of Jing province and was enfeoffed Marquis of Fubo.

sentences.zh: 二子：統、馥。

translations.literal: Two sons: Tong and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Tong and Fu.

sentences.zh: 十世孫孕，孕六世孫渠，渠生鉉，燕北平郡守。

translations.literal: The tenth-generation descendant was Yun; Yun's sixth-generation descendant was Qu; Qu begot Xuan, Governor of Beiping commandery in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ten generations later came Yun; six generations after Yun came Qu, whose son Xuan was Governor of Beiping in Yan.

sentences.zh: 生元壽，後魏武川鎮司馬，生惠嘏。

translations.literal: He begot Yuanshou, a Staff Commandant at Wuchuan garrison under Later Wei; Yuanshou begot Huigu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanshou served Later Wei as Staff Commandant at Wuchuan garrison and had a son Huigu.

sentences.zh: 觀王房本出渠孫興，後魏新平郡守。

translations.literal: The Prince-of-Guan Branch originally derived from Qu's grandson Xing, Governor of Xinping commandery under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince-of-Guan Branch stems from Qu's grandson Xing, who served Later Wei as Governor of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 生國，國孫紹，後周特賜姓屋呂引氏，隋初復舊。

translations.literal: He begot Guo; Guo's grandson was Shao, specially granted the surname Wuluyin under Later Zhou, and restored to the old surname at the beginning of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Guo had a grandson Shao, who was specially granted the surname Wuluyin under Later Zhou and resumed the original surname at the start of Sui.

sentences.zh: 後以士雄封觀王，號觀王房。

translations.literal: Later Shixiong was enfeoffed Prince of Guan, and the line was styled the Prince-of-Guan Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shixiong received the title Prince of Guan, and the line was called the Prince-of-Guan Branch.

sentences.zh: 孕五世孫贊，隋輔國將軍、河東公。

translations.literal: Yun's fifth-generation descendant was Zan, General Who Supports the State and Duke of Hedong under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations from Yun came Zan, who served Sui as General Who Supports the State and Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 生初，左光祿大夫、華山郡公。

translations.literal: He begot Chu, Grand Master of the Left Palace and Duke of Huashan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Chu, Grand Master of the Left Palace and Duke of Huashan commandery.

sentences.zh: 初裔孫播，世居扶風。

translations.literal: Chu's descendant Bo dwelt for generations at Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Chu named Bo lived for generations at Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 太尉震子奉，字季叔，後漢城門校尉、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhen's son Feng, styled Jishu, was Commandant of the Capital Gates and Secretariat Attendant under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhen's son Feng, styled Jishu, served Later Han as Commandant of the Capital Gates and Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 八世孫結，仕慕容氏中山相。

translations.literal: The eighth-generation descendant Jie served the Murong as Chancellor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations later, Jie served the Murong as Chancellor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 二子：珍、繼。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhen and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Zhen and Ji.

sentences.zh: 至順，徙居河中永樂，岐徙居原武。

translations.literal: Down to Shun, [the line] moved to Yongle in Hezhong; Qi moved to Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Shun the family had moved to Yongle in Hezhong; Qi moved to Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 越公房本出中山相結次子繼。
