translations.literal: The Duke-of-Yue Branch originally derived from Ji, second son of Jie, Chancellor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke-of-Yue Branch stems from Ji, second son of Jie, Chancellor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 生暉，洛州刺史，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: He begot Hui, Governor of Luo province, posthumously titled Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Hui, Governor of Luo province, posthumously titled Jian.

sentences.zh: 生河間太守恩，恩生越恭公鈞，號越公房。

translations.literal: He begot En, Governor of Hejian; En begot Jun, Duke Gong of Yue, and the line was styled the Duke-of-Yue Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son En, Governor of Hejian; En's son Jun received the title Duke Gong of Yue, and the line was called the Duke-of-Yue Branch.

sentences.zh: 楊氏宰相十一人。

translations.literal: Eleven chancellors of the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 恭仁、執柔、師道、炎、國忠、再思、綰、收、涉、弘武、嗣復。

translations.literal: Gongren, Zhirou, Shidao, Yan, Guozhong, Zaosi, Wan, Shou, She, Hongwu, and Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren, Zhirou, Shidao, Yan, Guozhong, Zaosi, Wan, Shou, She, Hongwu, and Sifu.

sentences.zh: 高高氏出自姜姓，齊太公六世孫文公赤，生公子高，孫傒，為齊上卿，與管仲合諸侯有功，桓公命傒以王父字為氏，食采於盧，謚曰敬仲，世為上卿。

translations.literal: Gao—the Gao clan derives from the Jiang surname; Chi, Duke Wen, sixth-generation descendant of Grand Duke Wang of Qi, begot Prince Gao; his grandson Xi served Qi as Senior Minister; joining Guan Zhong he gathered the feudal lords and had merit; Duke Huan ordered Xi to take his grandfather's style character as his clan name, received a fief at Lu, was posthumously titled Jingzhong, and for generations served as Senior Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gao—the Gao clan traces its line to the Jiang surname. Chi, Duke Wen, sixth-generation descendant of Grand Duke Wang of Qi, had a son Prince Gao; his grandson Xi rose to Senior Minister of Qi. Together with Guan Zhong he rallied the feudal lords to great effect; Duke Huan had him take his grandfather's style character Gao as clan name, with a fief at Lu. Posthumously titled Jingzhong, the line served as Senior Minister for generations.

sentences.zh: 敬仲生莊子虎，虎生傾子，傾子生宣子固，固生厚，厚生子麗，子麗生止，奔燕。

translations.literal: Jingzhong begot Master Zhuang Hu; Hu begot Qingzi; Qingzi begot Xuanzi Gu; Gu begot Hou; Hou begot Zili; Zili begot Zhi, who fled to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong had a son Master Zhuang Hu; Hu's line ran through Qingzi, Xuanzi Gu, Hou, and Zili to Zhi, who fled to Yan.

sentences.zh: 十世孫量，為宋司城，後入楚。

translations.literal: The tenth-generation descendant Liang served Song as Minister of Works and later entered Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Ten generations later, Liang served Song as Minister of Works and later entered Chu.

sentences.zh: 十世孫洪，後漢渤海太守，因居渤海蓨縣。

translations.literal: The tenth-generation descendant Hong was Governor of Bohai under Later Han and therefore dwelt at Tiao county in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Ten generations later, Hong served Later Han as Governor of Bohai and settled at Tiao county in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 洪四世孫襃，字宣仁，太子太傅。

translations.literal: Hong's fourth-generation descendant Bao, styled Xuanren, was Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations from Hong came Bao, styled Xuanren, who served as Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 襃孫承，字文休，國子祭酒、東莞太守。

translations.literal: Bao's grandson Cheng, styled Wenxiu, was Chancellor of the National University and Governor of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's grandson Cheng, styled Wenxiu, served as Chancellor of the National University and Governor of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 生延，字慶壽，漢中太守。

translations.literal: He begot Yan, styled Qingshou, Governor of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yan, styled Qingshou, who served as Governor of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 延生納，字孝才，魏尚書郎、東莞太守。

translations.literal: Yan begot Na, styled Xiaocai, Secretariat Gentleman and Governor of Dongguan under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Na, styled Xiaocai, served Wei as Secretariat Gentleman and Governor of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 納生達，字式遠，吏部郎中、江夏太守。

translations.literal: Na begot Da, styled Shiyuan, Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Governor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Na's son Da, styled Shiyuan, served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Governor of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 四子：約、乂、隱、漢。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yue, Yi, Yin, and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons: Yue, Yi, Yin, and Han.

sentences.zh: 隱，晉玄菟太守。

translations.literal: Yin was Governor of Xuantu under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yin served Jin as Governor of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 生慶，北燕太子詹事、司空。

translations.literal: He begot Qing, Chief Steward to the Crown Prince of Northern Yan and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Qing, who served Northern Yan as Chief Steward to the Crown Prince and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三子：展、敬、泰。

translations.literal: Three sons: Zhan, Jing, and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons: Zhan, Jing, and Tai.

sentences.zh: 展，後魏黃門侍郎，三都大官。

translations.literal: Zhan was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate under Later Wei and Chief Steward of the Three Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan served Later Wei as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Chief Steward of the Three Capitals.

sentences.zh: 二子：讜、頤。

translations.literal: Two sons: Dang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Dang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 讜，冀青二州中正、滄水康公。

translations.literal: Dang was Rectifier for Ji and Qing provinces and Duke Kang of Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: Dang served as Rectifier for Ji and Qing provinces and was enfeoffed Duke Kang of Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 二子：祚、祐。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zuo and You.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Zuo and You.

sentences.zh: 祐字子集，光祿大夫、建康靈侯。

translations.literal: You, styled Ziji, was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Marquis Ling of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: You, styled Ziji, served as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and was enfeoffed Marquis Ling of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 二子：和璧、振。

translations.literal: Two sons: Hebi and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Hebi and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 泰，北燕吏部尚書、中書令。

translations.literal: Tai was Minister of Personnel and Director of the Secretariat of Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Tai served Northern Yan as Minister of Personnel and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二子：韜、湖。

translations.literal: Two sons: Tao and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Tao and Hu.

sentences.zh: 京兆高氏，又有與北齊同祖，初居文安，後徙京兆。

translations.literal: The Gao clan of Jingzhao had another branch sharing ancestry with Northern Qi; they first dwelt at Wen'an and later moved to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Gao of Jingzhao was another branch sharing ancestry with Northern Qi; it first lived at Wen'an and later moved to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 晉陵高氏，本出吳丹楊太守高瑞。

translations.literal: The Gao clan of Jinling originally derived from Gao Rui, Governor of Danyang in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinling Gao originally stem from Gao Rui, Governor of Danyang in Wu.

sentences.zh: 初居廣陵，四世孫悝，徙秣陵，十三世孫子長。

translations.literal: They first dwelt at Guangling; the fourth-generation descendant Kui moved to Molin; the thirteenth-generation descendant was Zichang.
translations.idiomatic: The family first lived at Guangling; four generations later Kui moved to Molin; thirteen generations later came Zichang.

sentences.zh: 高氏宰相四人。

translations.literal: Four chancellors of the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Four men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 士廉、璩、郢、智周。

translations.literal: Shilian, Qu, Ying, and Zhizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian, Qu, Ying, and Zhizhou.

sentences.zh: 房房氏出自祁姓，舜封堯子丹朱於房，朱生陵，以國為氏。

translations.literal: Fang—the Fang clan derives from the Qi surname; Shun enfeoffed Yao's son Danzhu at Fang; Danzhu begot Ling, who took the state as his clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Fang—the Fang clan traces its line to the Qi surname. Shun enfeoffed Yao's son Danzhu at Fang; Danzhu's son Ling took the state name as his clan.

sentences.zh: 陵三十五世孫鍾，周昭王時食采靈壽。

translations.literal: Ling's thirty-fifth-generation descendant Zhong, in the time of King Zhao of Zhou, received a fief at Lingshou.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-five generations from Ling came Zhong, who in the reign of King Zhao of Zhou held a fief at Lingshou.

sentences.zh: 生沈，沈十二世孫漢常山太守雅，徙清河繹幕。

translations.literal: He begot Shen; Shen's twelfth-generation descendant Ya, Governor of Changshan under Han, moved to Yimo in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Shen; twelve generations later Ya served Han as Governor of Changshan and moved the family to Yimo in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 十一世孫植，後漢司空。

translations.literal: The eleventh-generation descendant Zhi was Minister of Works under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven generations later, Zhi served Later Han as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 植八代孫諶，隨慕容德南遷，因居濟南。

translations.literal: Zhi's eighth-generation descendant Chen, following Murong De south in migration, therefore dwelt at Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations from Zhi came Chen, who followed Murong De's southward migration and settled at Jinan.

sentences.zh: 四子：裕、坦、邃、熙，號「四祖」。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yu, Tan, Sui, and Xi, styled the "Four Ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Four sons: Yu, Tan, Sui, and Xi, called the "Four Ancestors."

sentences.zh: 裕孫後魏冀州刺史法壽。

translations.literal: Yu's grandson under Later Wei was Fa Shou, Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's grandson Fa Shou served Later Wei as Governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 孫翼，仕至鎮遠將軍，襲壯武伯。

translations.literal: His grandson Yi rose in office to General Who Pacifies the Distant and inherited the title Baron of Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yi rose to General Who Pacifies the Distant and inherited the title Baron of Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 二子：熊、豹。

translations.literal: Two sons: Xiong and Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Xiong and Bao.

sentences.zh: 熊字子彪，本州主簿，生彥謙。

translations.literal: Xiong, styled Zibiao, was chief clerk of the province; he begot Yanqian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, styled Zibiao, served as chief clerk of the province and had a son Yanqian.

sentences.zh: 河南房氏，晉初有房乾，本出清河，使北虜，留而不遣，虜俗謂「房」為「屋引」，因改為屋引氏。

translations.literal: The Fang clan of Henan—in early Jin there was Fang Gan, originally of Qinghe, sent to the northern barbarians and detained; in barbarian custom "Fang" was pronounced "Wuyin," so the name was changed to the Wuyin clan.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Henan Fang, in early Jin there was Fang Gan of Qinghe, sent on mission to the northern tribes and detained; in their speech "Fang" sounded like "Wuyin," so the clan name was changed to Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 乾子孫隨魏南遷，復為房氏，而河南猶有屋引氏，唐雲麾將軍、弘江府統軍、渭源縣公豐生，即其後也。

translations.literal: Gan's descendants followed Wei south in migration and again became the Fang clan; yet in Henan there remained the Wuyin clan—Feng Sheng, General of the Cloud-Banner Guard, Commander of the Hongjiang Prefecture Army, and Duke of Wuyuan county under Tang, was their descendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gan's descendants followed Wei's southward migration and resumed the Fang surname, but the Wuyin clan remained in Henan—Feng Sheng, General of the Cloud-Banner Guard, Commander of the Hongjiang Prefecture Army, and Duke of Wuyuan county under Tang, was their descendant.

sentences.zh: 房氏宰相三人。

translations.literal: Three chancellors of the Fang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Three men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 玄齡、融、琯。

translations.literal: Xuanling, Rong, and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling, Rong, and Guan.

sentences.zh: 宇文宇文氏出自匈奴南單于之裔。

translations.literal: Yuwen—the Yuwen clan derives from descendants of the Southern Chanyu of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen—the Yuwen clan traces its line to descendants of the Southern Chanyu of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 有葛烏兔為鮮卑君長，世襲大人，至普迴，因獵得玉璽，自以為天授也，俗謂「天子」為「宇文」，因號宇文氏。

translations.literal: There was Gewutu who was a Xianbei chieftain, inheriting the great chieftainship generation after generation; down to Puhui, while hunting he obtained a jade seal and considered it heaven-sent; in custom "Son of Heaven" was called "Yuwen," so they took Yuwen as clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Gewutu was a Xianbei chieftain whose line held the great chieftainship for generations; down to Puhui, who while hunting found a jade seal and took it as a heaven-sent mandate—in their speech "Son of Heaven" was called "Yuwen," and the clan took that name.

sentences.zh: 或云神農氏為黃帝所滅，子孫遁居北方。

translations.literal: Some say the Shennong clan was destroyed by the Yellow Emperor and descendants hid in the north.
translations.idiomatic: One account holds that the Shennong clan was destroyed by the Yellow Emperor and its descendants fled north.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑俗呼「草」為「俟汾」，以神農有嘗草之功，因自號俟汾氏，其後音訛遂為宇文氏。

translations.literal: In Xianbei custom grass was called "Sirun"; because Shennong had the merit of tasting herbs, they styled themselves the Sirun clan; later the pronunciation shifted and it became Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianbei speech grass was called "Sirun"; because Shennong had the merit of tasting herbs, they styled themselves the Sirun clan, and later the pronunciation shifted to Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 普迴子莫那自陰山徙居遼西，至後周追謚曰獻侯。

translations.literal: Puhui's son Monuo moved from Yinshan to Liaoxi; under Later Zhou he was posthumously titled Marquis Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui's son Monuo moved from Yinshan to Liaoxi; under Later Zhou he was posthumously enfeoffed Marquis Xian.

sentences.zh: 獻侯生可地汗，號莫何單于，闢地西出玉門，東踰遼水。

translations.literal: Marquis Xian begot Kedihan, styled Mohe Chanyu; he opened territory west beyond Yumenguan and east beyond the Liao River.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Xian's son Kedihan, styled Mohe Chanyu, opened territory west beyond Yumenguan and east beyond the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 孫普撥，普撥生丘不勤，丘不勤生莫珪，莫珪生遜昵延，遜昵延生佚豆歸，自稱大單于，為慕容晃所滅。

translations.literal: His grandson Pubo; Pubo begot Qiubuqin; Qiubuqin begot Mogui; Mogui begot Xunniyan; Xunniyan begot Yidougui, who styled himself Great Chanyu and was destroyed by Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Pubo; Pubo's line ran through Qiubuqin, Mogui, and Xunniyan to Yidougui, who styled himself Great Chanyu and was destroyed by Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 生六子：一曰拔拔陵陵，二曰拔拔瓌，三曰紇闍，四曰目原，五曰紇闍俟直，六曰目陳。

translations.literal: He begot six sons: first Babaling Ling, second Babao Gui, third Hechan, fourth Muyuan, fifth Hechan Shizhi, sixth Muchen.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: first Babaling Ling, second Babao Gui, third Hechan, fourth Muyuan, fifth Hechan Shizhi, sixth Muchen.

sentences.zh: 拔拔陵陵號阿若諺，仕後魏，都牧主、開府儀同三司、安定忠侯，以豪傑徙居代州武川。

translations.literal: Babaling Ling, styled Aruoyan, served Later Wei as Chief Herdsman, General with the privileges of the Three Divisions, and Marquis Zhong of Anding; as a man of eminent ability he moved to Wuchuan in Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Babaling Ling, styled Aruoyan, served Later Wei as Chief Herdsman and General with the privileges of the Three Divisions and was enfeoffed Marquis Zhong of Anding; as a man of eminent ability he moved to Wuchuan in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 生系，位至內阿干。

translations.literal: He begot Xi, who rose to the office of Neigan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Xi, who rose to the office of Neigan.

sentences.zh: 二子：韜、阿頭。

translations.literal: Two sons: Tao and Atou.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Tao and Atou.

sentences.zh: 韜三子：肱、顥、泰。

translations.literal: Tao's three sons: Gong, Hao, and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had three sons: Gong, Hao, and Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰，後周太祖文皇帝。

translations.literal: Tai was the Founding Literary Emperor, Taizu of Later Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was Emperor Wen, founding emperor of Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 阿頭生仲，贈大司徒、虞公。

translations.literal: Atou begot Zhong, posthumously enfeoffed Grand Minister of Education and Duke of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Atou's son Zhong was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Minister of Education and Duke of Yu.

sentences.zh: 生興，襲虞公，生洛。

translations.literal: He begot Xing, who inherited Duke of Yu; Xing begot Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Xing, who inherited the title Duke of Yu; Xing's son was Luo.

sentences.zh: 目原孫跋，後魏羽真尚書、居庸侯。

translations.literal: Muyuan's grandson Ba served Later Wei as Yuzhen Secretariat Director and Marquis of Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: Muyuan's grandson Ba served Later Wei as Yuzhen Secretariat Director and was enfeoffed Marquis of Juyong.

sentences.zh: 生直力勤，比部尚書。

translations.literal: He begot Zhiliqin, Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Zhiliqin, who served as Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 直力勤生賢。

translations.literal: Zhiliqin begot Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiliqin's son was Xian.

sentences.zh: 又有費也頭氏，臣屬鮮卑佚豆歸，後從其主亦稱宇文氏。

translations.literal: There was also the Feiyetou clan, vassals subordinate to the Xianbei Yidougui; later following their lord they also styled themselves the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Feiyetou clan, vassals of the Xianbei Yidougui; later, following their lord, they too took the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 仕後魏，世為沃野鎮軍主，玄孫盛。

translations.literal: Serving Later Wei, for generations they were garrison commanders at Woye; the great-great-grandson was Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Later Wei, they held the post of garrison commander at Woye for generations; the great-great-grandson was Sheng.

sentences.zh: 宇文氏宰相三人。

translations.literal: Three chancellors of the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Three men of this clan served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 士及、節、融。

translations.literal: Shiji, Jie, and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji, Jie, and Rong.
